description:
Commands that cannot run without Git report that through one typed error and one error code, so claims and hook installation classify the same condition the same way.

## Background

Claim and lease commands report a missing or unusable Git repository through `ClaimRequiresGitError`, classified as `CLAIM_REQUIRES_GIT`. `jit hooks install` needs a Git repository too, but it has no matching code. Its handler reports the condition as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (exit 2) as an interim mapping, because the failure-probe contract rejects untyped failures. Nothing the user passed is invalid, so that code misclassifies the condition.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One error type and one error code name a command's requirement for Git, independent of the command family. `ClaimRequiresGitError` and `CLAIM_REQUIRES_GIT` no longer exist, and nothing aliases or maps the old code.
- [hard] REQ-02: Claim and lease commands that need Git report the new code with the exit status the old code had, and carry the same remediation detail.
- [hard] REQ-03: `jit hooks install` outside a Git repository reports the new code. The interim `INVALID_ARGUMENT` mapping for that condition is removed from its handler, its exit-code row and the exit-code reference.
- [hard] REQ-04: The error-code reference, the exit-code reference, and the generated command schema state the new code, and no document or test names the removed one.
- [hard] REQ-05: Tests assert the new code and exit status for one claim command and for `hooks install` outside Git, on both the human and the machine-readable path.

## Notes

Steward ruling (2026-11-04): the interim `INVALID_ARGUMENT` mapping for `hooks install` lands with the wave 7 handler batch, and this task ends it. The repository has no backward-compatibility obligation (`@/inv/canonical-cutover`).
title: One requires-Git error for every command family
